solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Position at match containing leaders of team under duress

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for a match holds the next letters within it

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture in a cup competition

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A team's position in a fixture when its captains are under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie is a cup match; 'leaders of' takes the first letter of each of the three words and 'containing' sets them within the match.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude can mean a physical posture or stance, a synonym for position.

clue.text: Circular yard with quiet surrounded by set of cars

indicators.note: the yard and quiet letters sit inside the word for a set of cars

parts.note: a fleet is a company's collection of vehicles
SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Looks like a car-park puzzle: a round yard, kept quiet, ringed with vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like an adjective describing the yard, but it is the noun, a printed handout.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular is a printed leaflet handed out widely, which is what a flysheet is.

clue.text: A pass yet to be constructed for assistant

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: the following letters are still to be built, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone waiting for a permit that has not yet been built to hire a helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be constructed' rearranges only the word yet; A and the pass stand as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is a helper or attendant, originally one serving a priest at the altar.

clue.text: Part of song that's difficult to bear

definitions.meaning: an old word for the refrain or chorus of a song
a load or responsibility that weighs heavily on someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a song's refrain and a heavy load that one has to carry.

clue.text: Judge in Spain boarding a pair of ships

indicators.note: the letter for Spain gets on board, going between the two ships

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, so two ships give SS twice
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A Spanish judge climbs aboard one of two vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarding' puts the letter for Spain between the two ships.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to evaluate it, to judge its worth or quality.

clue.text: Ablest recruit mobilised in warship

indicators.note: set in motion and reorganised, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: The most capable new sailor is called up to serve on a fighting ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A battlecruiser is a large, fast type of armoured naval vessel, a kind of warship.

clue.text: Do-gooder providing worry for cardiologist?

definitions.meaning: a soft-hearted liberal, too ready to sympathise
read literally, a heart that is losing blood is a medical concern for a heart doctor

explanation.surface: A charitable type causing a heart specialist concern.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a disparaging term for an excessively sympathetic liberal, a do-gooder.

clue.text: Nuts and set of drinks before dance

parts.note: a round is drinks bought for everyone in a group at once
the twist is a 1960s dance craze

explanation.surface: A night out: snacks and a round of drinks before hitting the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like bar snacks beside the drinks, but it is the definition, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Going round the twist is British slang for going mad, so nuts in the sense of crazy.

clue.text: Information is found about university egghead

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the word is goes round the letter for university

explanation.surface: News that a clever academic has been discovered at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information; 'found' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an intellectual, someone of great intelligence like a genius.

clue.text: Distribute generously pounds with a lot due for review

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

indicators.note: material sent back to be looked at again and revised, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone handing over money freely while a large sum is up for audit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for review' rearranges LOT DUE into DLEOUT, after L and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To ladle out is to dish something out in large amounts, as with soup from a ladle.

clue.text: Odd bits of heavy farm material?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are picked from the next word

explanation.surface: Heavy bits of farm material seem to be the topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits of' takes letters 1, 3 and 5 of heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay is dried grass, a bulky material found on every farm, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bring forward in discussion poster scheduled around cinema's opening

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement such as a poster

indicators.note: the word for scheduled wraps round the next letter

parts.note: something due is expected at a set time

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone raising a cinema poster schedule at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring forward in discussion' is the definition, a formal way to say cite as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite or offer something as evidence in an argument.

clue.text: Northern area with settled density inhabited by English?

indicators.note: the word density takes the letter for English inside it
arranged and fixed in place, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A northern district with a settled, dense population that is largely English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhabited by' adds E to DENSITY; 'settled' rearranges the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyneside is the conurbation around the River Tyne, Newcastle and Gateshead, in north-east England.

clue.text: Period recalled in spectacular exhibition

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction
the letters sit within the next two words

explanation.surface: A period remembered through a spectacular show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds ARE across spectacular exhibition; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a historical period, an age marked by some distinctive character.

clue.text: Thoroughly describing diver's place of work?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a diver works far down below the surface of the water

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means comprehensively, and literally names the deep water where a diver operates.

clue.text: Trophy that may be made in a frame?

definitions.meaning: a cup awarded as a prize, slang for silverware

definitions.text: may be made in a frame?
definitions.meaning: in snooker, a frame is one game, during which a player sinks balls

explanation.definitionFit: A pot is slang for a sporting cup, and potting a ball is a shot in a snooker frame.

clue.text: Loaded term for criminality after reforming the law

indicators.note: the final letter comes after the rearranged letters
forming again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
a term is an end, so the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A rich person's word for crime once the legal system is overhauled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' turns THE LAW into WEALTH; 'term for' gives Y, the last letter of criminality.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very rich, having plenty of money.

clue.text: Local beer largely drunk getting seal of approval from Greens?

indicators.note: intoxicated and in disarray, so the letters are jumbled
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Green campaigners give a seal of approval to a local brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts beer to BEE; 'drunk' rearranges LOCAL plus BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecolabel is a mark certifying a product as environmentally friendly, approved by green campaigners.

clue.text: Capital type of fellow detained by solitary figure

indicators.note: held inside the word for the solitary figure

parts.note: a loner is someone who prefers to be alone
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A college fellow held prisoner by a reclusive character.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is an Oxbridge college fellow, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A Londoner is a resident of London, the UK capital, so a capital type.

clue.text: Cameron, say, with European in Nato squabbles

indicators.note: quarrels throw things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Former Prime Minister David Cameron arguing with a European at NATO.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squabbles' rearranges IN NATO into TONIAN, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron was educated at Eton College, so he is an example of an Old Etonian.

clue.text: Severe work by barber a useful expedient?

parts.note: short can mean curt and severe in manner
a cut is a haircut given by a barber

explanation.surface: A barber's harsh trim turns out to be a handy trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcut is a quicker method of getting something done, a convenient expedient.

clue.text: Consideration shown in rare garden

indicators.note: the letters are on display within the next two words

explanation.surface: Admiration expressed for an unusual garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Regard means attention or respect paid to something, a synonym for consideration.

clue.text: Fancy practice session for instrument

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like fancy that
in cricket, nets are practice sessions in netted enclosures

explanation.surface: An elaborate rehearsal for a musician's instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an adjective but is the exclamation, as in 'Fancy that!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornet is a brass instrument similar to a small trumpet.

clue.text: Speak about number in flowery fashion

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective used predicatively

indicators.note: the word for speak goes round the letter for number

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally, making a speech

explanation.surface: Making a speech about figures in an elaborate style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside ORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, flowery in style, especially of language.

clue.text: Valuable commodity taken back in rebellion

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards
the letters lie within the next word

explanation.surface: A precious resource recaptured during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds LIO inside rebellion; 'taken back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is a valuable traded commodity, crude petroleum sold on world markets.

clue.text: Dependant with titled figure restraining rage

indicators.note: holding in, so the word for rage is put inside

parts.note: Hon is short for Honourable, a title given to certain nobles
anger means fury or rage

explanation.surface: A dependent relative with an aristocratic title keeping their temper in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Hon, for Honourable, is a courtesy title borne by children of peers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who depends on someone for favours.

clue.text: A party attracting lust, say, upset handsome figure

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: overturned, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins, an example of sin

explanation.surface: Lust at a party disturbs a good-looking guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting' is a link word; 'upset' reverses only the example of a deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was a beautiful youth in Greek myth, so his name means a very handsome man.

clue.text: Equestrian competition in long weekend?

definitions.meaning: a horse trials contest of dressage, cross-country and showjumping
read literally, a weekend extended to include an extra day

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a horse trials contest, and literally an occasion lasting three days, like a long weekend.
